description: ESP32-S3 + 8MB PSRAM + OV2640 camera + PDM mic + microSD
why: Runs firmware/ring-esp32s3 unmodified; proves capture → BLE → phone → LLM → spoken answer (headphones or the optional ring speaker) plus haptic/LED cues end to end
notes: Some units ship with OV3660; both supported

why: Crisp haptic cues (listening / answer ready) with closed-loop LRA drive; optional silent Morse mode
notes: Or DRV2605LDGS bare chip on LCSC ~$1.34

description: e.g. Precision Microdrives C08-005 or Jameco 8 mm LRA
why: Primary cue channel (haptic ticks; optional silent Morse)

description: e.g. Murata PKMCS0909E4000-R1 (LTB) or any 12 mm passive piezo
why: Audible beep cues (optional; off by default — cues_mask bit 2)

description: Adafruit 1570 (31 x 11.5 x 3.8 mm) for bench battery tests
notes: XIAO has an on-board charger (BAT pads)

description: Battery sense divider to A0: BAT+ → 100 k → A0 → 100 k → GND with 100 nF on A0 (hardware/pcb/wiring_stage0.md)
why: Battery % in status; ~20 µA drain (10 k/10 k would be 210 µA)

description: Adafruit 3006: MAX98357A class-D mono amp, 2.5-5.5 V, screw terminal for the speaker; wire BCLK → D7/GPIO44, LRC → D6/GPIO43, DIN → D10/GPIO9, SD → 3V3, VIN → 3V3, GND → GND (hardware/pcb/wiring_stage0.md)
why: Hear the answer from the ring (BLE AUDIO_OUT stream → I2S) instead of the phone; same amp as the stage-1 board
notes: D10 was PIN_AUX (the air-puff experiment is parked on the dev kit, config_audio.h). GAIN open = 9 dB clips the top ~1.7 dB at 3.3 V — keep the volume <= 200, or wire GAIN → VIN through 100 k for the stage-1 board's 3 dB (clean at 255)

description: PUI AS01008MR-2-R (10 mm, 8 ohm, 300 mW) — the stage-1 part; or a 1 W 8 ohm oval such as Adafruit 3923 for the bench
why: Load for the amp breakout at the loudness the ring will have (~66 dB at 1 m with the 10 mm driver)
notes: Solder 2 leads to the screw terminal; polarity irrelevant
